value.hook: When adding assistant-text renderers or reviewing streaming display hooks
value.title: Price renderers per draw, not per turn

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Separate RPC frequency from renderer frequency. In #212 at 68ecd89, an ordinary turn makes no turn-end RPC, yet every assistant-text draw still splits/scans the whole reply. Hidden blocks also rebuild the prose prefix. With B bytes and D draws, added work follows the sum of rendered prefix sizes, potentially quadratic cumulative work for fixed-size streaming increments, plus transient arrays/strings. Static replies are rescanned whenever the host invokes the renderer. A command-count cap and a launch-free extension do not bound this UI cost.

Name the draw rate, text size, allocations and cache/memoization boundary before calling a renderer cheap. Small behavior fixtures and a flat process counter establish neither long-reply latency nor allocation pressure; source complexity is not a measured cost breach. Under C34, name that proof gap as a follow-up unless normal-use failure is established.

Also distinguish a permanent tick from per-attempt timers: this adapter has a 25 s RPC deadline and a 50 ms idle-wait chain capped at 40 timers after a block attempt. Those are real costs even though no global polling loop was added.

Review and feature-off baseline: output c891d789. Current obligations live in handover 8a92ec54, not this durable lesson.
